findings.corrective_action: Atomically transition each position from OPEN to EXIT_CLAIMED before external calls, use a unique durable attempt record, serialize nonce allocation per chain and wallet, and reconcile the claimed transaction before allowing another exit.
findings.deterministic_evidence: The source contains no pre-broadcast state transition in close_position; _DB_LOCK first appears after fee handling and after the SELL receipt.

evidence.detail: close_position reads an OPEN position at lines 1128-1133, broadcasts the SELL at 1141, and only acquires _DB_LOCK to mark it closed at 1170. There is no durable pre-broadcast claim or compare-and-set transition.
The independent intelligence worker calls close_position at line 540 while the SiBot live worker also invokes close_position from monitoring and leader-event paths.
_base_tx obtains the pending nonce independently at line 304; no wallet-scoped nonce lock or durable nonce reservation surrounds signing and broadcast.

findings.impact: Concurrent monitor/event paths can both observe OPEN, build transactions from the same balance, and broadcast competing or sequential SELLs. Shared-wallet operations can also reuse a nonce, causing replacement, failure, or unintended ordering.
findings.root_cause: The database lock protects only the final accounting update, not the complete claim-build-broadcast-reconcile state machine.
tests_required: Race two close_position callers and assert exactly one broadcast.
Crash after broadcast but before position update and verify restart reconciliation.
Run concurrent operations for one EVM wallet and verify unique monotonic nonces.
findings.title: EVM position exits can be submitted more than once

findings.corrective_action: Persist BROADCAST/RECONCILING plus transaction hash before waiting for a receipt. Resolve receipts and balance deltas asynchronously, prohibit retries while outcome is unknown, and distinguish failed-before-send from unknown-after-send.
findings.deterministic_evidence: The exception row literal sets tx_hash to an empty string even when txh was assigned before wait_for_transaction_receipt.

evidence.detail: After execute_cycle returns a transaction hash, receipt timeout raises at lines 217-219. The broad handler at 241-243 then writes status REJECTED with an empty tx_hash.
close_position broadcasts at line 1141 and waits at 1142, but a timeout leaves the position OPEN without persisting the transaction hash or a reconciling state.
Eligibility/cooldown accounting counts broadcast-like statuses, but not REJECTED, so the ambiguous attempt does not prevent a later cycle from submitting again.

findings.impact: A transaction accepted by the node but not confirmed within the local timeout can execute on-chain while local state says REJECTED or OPEN. Subsequent cycles can repeat the trade, and realised P&L, exposure, fees, and notifications become incorrect.
findings.root_cause: Broadcast and confirmation are treated as one operation; the transaction identity is not durably recorded immediately after send.
tests_required: Simulate send success followed by receipt timeout and assert durable RECONCILING state with the hash.
Restart and reconcile both successful and reverted transactions.
Assert no second execution occurs while an attempt is unresolved.
findings.title: Ambiguous EVM broadcasts are recorded as rejected and may be retried

findings.corrective_action: Move authorization and activation state to SQLite with BEGIN IMMEDIATE and a conditional uses < max_uses update, or introduce a process-wide plus OS-level file lock and re-read under that lock.
findings.deterministic_evidence: Unlike operator_control.py, user_registry.py declares no lock and performs every authorization mutation as an unlocked CSV read/replace sequence.

evidence.detail: redeem_activation_code reads the CSV, checks uses, increments it in memory, and replaces the file at lines 179-206 without any lock, file lock, transaction, or atomic compare-and-set.
join_user, update_user, set_user_setting, and activation writes use the same unlocked read-modify-replace pattern.
Telegram handling is extended by multiple worker threads and callbacks, making concurrent redemptions and settings writes feasible.

findings.impact: Two users can redeem a nominally single-use activation code concurrently and both become active. Concurrent user or trading-setting writes can also silently overwrite one another.
findings.root_cause: CSV replacement provides atomic file visibility but not atomic read-modify-write semantics.
tests_required: Synchronize two concurrent redemptions of a one-use code and assert exactly one succeeds.
Exercise concurrent creation and settings updates without lost rows.
Add a multi-process locking test, not only a thread test.
findings.title: Activation-code use limits are not atomic

findings.corrective_action: Separate accrued_fee from paid_fee, store the transaction hash and nonce durably, confirm the receipt and balance transfer before marking PAID, and implement idempotent retry/reconciliation for PENDING or ambiguous fees.
findings.deterministic_evidence: No code path updates fee-ledger BROADCAST/PENDING rows to confirmed or failed, while P&L immediately subtracts the proposed fee.

evidence.detail: A fee transfer is considered BROADCAST immediately at lines 1157-1163. user_net and cumulative profit_fee are reduced by the fee at 1165-1172 whether the transfer confirms or remains PENDING.
The fee transfer at lines 228-239 is never receipt-confirmed; the trade is labelled SUCCESS whenever send_raw_transaction returns, and no settlement worker is present.
fee_ledger.csv only appends BROADCAST/PENDING records; repository search found no fee reconciliation or retry implementation.

findings.impact: Reported user net, master fee revenue, and fee liabilities diverge from on-chain balances when a fee transaction is replaced, reverted, dropped, or never sent. Pending fees can remain permanently unsettled.
findings.root_cause: Accounting recognizes fee settlement at submission time and lacks a durable receivable/reconciliation lifecycle.
tests_required: Cover confirmed, reverted, dropped, timed-out, and failed-before-send fee transfers.
Verify gross P&L, user-net P&L, accrued fees, and paid fees reconcile independently.
Verify restart recovery cannot charge a fee twice.
findings.title: Profit-share liabilities are booked as paid without confirmation or recovery

findings.corrective_action: Make portfolio/report evaluation pure; persist decisions only on an explicit scheduled evaluation when inputs changed. Split get_or_create from register_new_version and never reset an existing lifecycle status during lookup.
findings.deterministic_evidence: The nominal report call deterministically executes UPDATE and INSERT statements for every strategy.

evidence.detail: The master-only report calls portfolio_report at line 31 and describes itself as recording-only/read-only.
portfolio_report calls evaluate_strategy for every registered strategy at lines 472-479. evaluate_strategy updates registry status and inserts a new decision row on every call at 458-468.
Cache-cold strategy lookup invokes register_strategy at lines 50-65; register_strategy increments version and resets existing status to SHADOW in strategy_lab.py lines 194-220.

findings.impact: Opening a report changes strategy lifecycle state and adds duplicate decisions. Process restarts or first events can increment versions and erase REPLACE/REWORK/PROMOTION_CANDIDATE status back to SHADOW, undermining the live sizing throttle and growing SQLite indefinitely.
findings.root_cause: Queries, evaluation persistence, and idempotent strategy lookup are conflated.
tests_required: Assert repeated report rendering produces no database writes.
Assert restart/cache loss does not change version or status.
Assert a new version is created only when the canonical strategy specification changes.
Add bounded retention or deduplication for decision history.
findings.title: Read-only Strategy Lab reports mutate lifecycle state and grow the database

findings.corrective_action: Use a minimal preflight job to read control and report signatures first, dispatch adjudication only on material change, use shallow/API-only retrieval where possible, pin and cache provider CLIs, and bound cache/worktree/artifact retention without deleting databases, wallets, or audit evidence.
findings.deterministic_evidence: Workflow step ordering unconditionally places installation before both the lane gate and the unchanged-report gate.

evidence.detail: The workflow runs every five minutes with a two-lane matrix. Each job performs full-history checkout and installs requirements plus four @latest AI CLIs at lines 44-70 before reading lane controls or checking the unchanged-report signature at lines 72-229.

Deterministic inventory at this commit reports 36 scheduled workflows, 11 scheduled self-hosted workflows, 22 full-history checkouts, 38 latest CLI installs, 23 npm installs, 58 pip installs, and 47 paid-AI-signalling workflows.
Root filesystem is 84.54% used with 2,157,146,112 bytes free. Host-wide network delta was approximately 968.92 MB/hour; attribution to this bot alone is not available.

findings.impact: The selected-master schedule can create up to 576 matrix jobs per day that download dependencies and full history even when disabled or already adjudicated. This wastes GitHub/network resources and increases cache/worktree pressure on an already constrained VPS ecosystem.
findings.root_cause: Cheap control/material-change gates occur after checkout, setup, and tool installation; provider CLIs are installed unpinned on every run.
tests_required: Workflow test proving unchanged reports skip checkout and all package installs.
Workflow test proving disabled lanes create no matrix worker.
Measure per-run downloaded bytes, cache growth, and retained worktrees.
Verify optimization preserves all trading and safety controls.
findings.title: High-frequency adjudication installs every provider CLI before determining that no work is needed
